sectors.trend: Earnings divergence: AI infrastructure (Dell, TSMC, Palo Alto) outperforms; application-layer (Credo, Coupang, Shopify) lags. Nvidia's $3.5B Qualcomm-rival investment signals AI chip consolidation.
sectors.implications: Rotation from speculative AI names to proven infrastructure plays. Citi recommends buying tumbling tech—contrarian entry window possible.

sectors.trend: Oil surges on Iran strikes; Ghana courts upstream investors post Shell-Chevron deal. Offshore energy spending recovering (Oceaneering).
sectors.implications: Energy hedges gain value; inflation pass-through to consumer goods accelerates. BYD overseas strategy outperforms Tesla in Europe.

sectors.trend: Yen intervention risk, USD at 2-week high, Singapore dollar favored. ING ordered to add capital in Australia. Partners Group CEO change signals private-market stress.
sectors.implications: Carry-trade unwind risk elevated. Global dollar exposure (headline 5) creates systemic fragility. BNS beats profit target—banking resilience.

sectors.trend: Five Below lifts outlook targeting Gen Alpha; Petco turnaround continues; Poundland to be sold; Denny's rival bankrupt; Warby Parker underwhelms.
sectors.implications: Bifurcation: value/discount retailers resilient, mid-tier discretionary under stress. Labor Day sales (headline 53) may provide near-term volume support.

sectors.trend: Congo Ebola outbreak with 'ghost pay' disputes hamper response; LeMaitre Vascular speculative pullback; Atmus Filtration Q2 pressure.
sectors.implications: Pandemic-preparedness stocks may see event-driven spikes; biotech remains volatile with speculative overhang.

key_themes: Yen intervention risk and global FX realignment
Iran conflict driving oil/inflation spike vs. weak US labor data
US bond selloff and rising yields pressuring equities
Global rotation: out of US equities, into Japan and Singapore
AI infrastructure vs. application-layer earnings divergence
Consumer discretionary stress amid inflation pass-through
Private-market redemptions and growth fatigue (Uber, Partners Group)
Climate vulnerability (Nepal flooding) as long-term infrastructure risk
China delivery sector revival on Meituan estimate surge

risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce JPY short exposure; hedge USD/JPY above 155; monitor BOJ intervention signals. Bessent's 'stronger yen' comment (51) suggests coordinated policy shift.
Maintain energy hedges (XLE, USO); reduce duration in rate-sensitive sectors. Iran strikes (48) could push Brent above $90.
Shorten bond duration; favor TIPS. Japan 30Y auction (9) adds global debt stress. Fed's Barr open to hike (68) removes rate-cut tailwind.
ADP 38K (25) is concerning but single data point. Monitor NFP Sept 5. Maintain quality earnings exposure (TSM, BNS).
Gold as hedge (6); energy sector overweight. Monitor Strait of Hormuz shipping costs.
Avoid evergreen fund exposure; Uber layoffs (26) and Partners Group CEO change (57, 75) signal broader growth-sector de-rating.
Nepal flooding (17) and Congo Ebola (2) are tail risks; maintain diversified geographic exposure.

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight Japanese equities; reduce US large-cap tech
opportunities.rationale: Natixis rotation (3), yen strength, and Japan's relative value vs. US multiples. Citi's 'buy tumbling tech' (45) suggests contrarian entry in quality names.

opportunities.recommendation: Add Singapore dollar exposure; favor SGD-denominated assets
opportunities.rationale: USD debasement narrative (4) and global dollar overexposure (5) favor SGD as safe-haven alternative.

opportunities.recommendation: Buy energy hedges and gold on Iran-driven oil spike
opportunities.rationale: Oil surge (48) + inflation fears + gold holding gains (6) create favorable risk/reward for commodity exposure.

opportunities.recommendation: Position in Chinese delivery/logistics on Meituan estimate surge
opportunities.rationale: 500% estimate jump (7) could catalyze sector re-rating; Meituan, iQIYI, and logistics peers benefit.

opportunities.recommendation: Add Australian equities on earnings inflection
opportunities.rationale: First earnings beat in 4 years (18) signals cyclical turning point; BNS beats profit target (50).

opportunities.recommendation: Consider AI infrastructure over application-layer names
opportunities.rationale: Nvidia $3.5B investment (65), TSMC stellar results (63), Dell beat (43) vs. Credo/Coupang misses (41, 59).

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce USD long exposure; hedge with JPY/SGD
defensive_moves.rationale: Global dollar overexposure (5) + yen intervention risk (1, 19, 51) + USD debasement (4) create asymmetric downside.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Shorten bond duration; favor TIPS over nominal Treasuries
defensive_moves.rationale: Bond selloff (9, 51) + Fed hike optionality (68) + oil-driven inflation (48) pressure nominal yields.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Trim speculative/growth exposure; avoid evergreen private funds
defensive_moves.rationale: Uber layoffs (26), Partners Group CEO change (57, 75), Shopify compression (56) signal growth de-rating.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Maintain 10-15% gold allocation as geopolitical hedge
defensive_moves.rationale: Iran conflict (48), yen uncertainty (1), and inflation fears (30) support gold's safe-haven bid.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Avoid consumer discretionary mid-tier; favor value/discount
defensive_moves.rationale: Denny's rival bankruptcy (47), Poundland sale (27), Warby Parker miss (74) vs. Five Below/Petco strength (11, 12).

market_outlook.short_term: High volatility expected. Yen intervention risk + oil spike + bond selloff create a 'risk-off' tape. Dow below key level (38) signals further downside unless oil stabilizes. ADP weakness (25) vs. hawkish Fed (68) creates policy uncertainty. Expect 3-5% equity drawdown risk in 1-2 weeks.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook cautiously constructive if Iran de-escalates and yen stabilizes. AI infrastructure capex cycle (Nvidia, TSMC) remains intact. Australian and Japanese earnings inflections offer diversification. Inflation pass-through from oil (30) may delay rate cuts to Q1 2027. Structural shift toward SGD/JPY from USD is multi-quarter.

Fed Barr speech / rate hike signal
